costs.heading: Cost of Sales and Operating Expenses
costs.text: The table below sets forth a comparison of cost of sales and operating expenses for the relevant periods presented.

rd.text: Research and development (“R&D”) expenses for t he three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, increased by $8.3 million, or 28.5%, and $23.2 million, or 37.2%, respectively, compared to the corresponding prior-year periods. The increases were primarily driven by continued investment in support of Keenova's core products, Acthar Gel and XIAFLEX, as well as the inclusion of three and nine months of expenses from the combined business in the current-year periods, respectively, compared to two months in the corresponding prior-year periods following the Business Combination.

nonint.heading: Cost of Sales and Operating Expenses
nonint.text: The table below sets forth a comparison of cost of sales and operating expenses for the relevant periods presented.

nonop.text: Interest expense during t he three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, increased by $0.6 million, or 1.2%, and $37.7 million, or 32.8%, respectively, compared to the corresponding prior-year periods. The increases were driven by higher average outstanding debt balances reflecting the assumption of Endo’s outstanding debt obligations in connection with the Business Combination, partially offset by lower coupon interest rates on the assumed debt compared to the “second-out” senior secured takeback term loans and “second-out” 14.75% senior secured first lien notes outstanding in the prior-year periods.

tax.text: We recognized income tax benefits of $20.0 million and $38.2 million on losses from continuing operations before income taxes of $116.1 million and $468.3 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. This resulted in an effective tax rate of 17.2% and 8.2%, respectively. The effective tax rate differs from the Irish statutory tax rate of 12.5%, predominantly due to return-to-provision adjustments and non-deductible expenses, including interest, compensation, and costs associated with the Business Combination, integration, and other related expenses.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Net cash provided by operating activities was $290.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, consisting of loss from continuing operations of $430.1 million adjusted for non-cash charges of $782.0 million and changes in working capital that used $61.9 million. Non-cash adjustments primarily included inventory fair value step-up amortization from acquisitions of $271.7 million, the non-restructuring impairment charge of $207.7 million, depreciation and amortization of $172.7 million, loss on divestiture of $150.3 million, and share-based compensation expense of $45.3 million, partially offset by changes in deferred income tax of $76.4 million. The change in working capital was primarily driven by net cash outflows of $95.1 million relating to increased accounts receivable, net, $33.7 million for the Acthar Gel-Related Settlement and $13.2 million for contingent consideration partially offset by a $75.3 million net cash provided by changes to other assets and liabilities.

Net cash used in operating activities was $41.1 million for the nine months ended September 26, 2025, consisting of loss from continuing operations of $347.7 million adjusted for non-cash charges of $177.6 million and changes in working capital that provided $129.0 million.

intro.text: Keenova Therapeutics is a leading U.S.-focused branded therapeutics company that strives to help patients with rare or unaddressed conditions live happier and healthier lives. Keenova’s rare disease capabilities underpin our diversified brands portfolio, which is focused across a wide range of specialty therapeutic areas of significant unmet need. These include rheumatology, ophthalmology, nephrology, neurology, pulmonology, orthopedics, urology, and neonatal respiratory critical care.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

• Our business depends on the continued effectiveness of our information technology infrastructure, and external attacks or any failures could harm our operations.
Generally, our business relies upon patent and trade-secret protection to protect our products, related inventions, and product innovations that are important to our business.
The protection afforded, which may also vary from country to country, depends upon the type of patent, its scope of coverage, and the availability of meaningful legal remedies in the country.
In addition, commercial durability may also partially depend upon product-related trade secrets, confidentiality agreements, know-how, and trademark and copyright laws.

Any person that files a Section 505(b)(2) NDA, the type of NDA that relies upon the data in the application for which the patents are listed, or an ANDA to secure approval of a generic version of a previous drug, must make a certification in respect to listed patents.
The determination of when generic exclusivity begins and ends is very complicated as it depends on several different factors.

CMS may use these submissions to determine payment rates for drugs under Medicare Part B. Since 2023, manufacturers must pay refunds to Medicare for single source drugs or biologics, or biosimilar biological products, reimbursed under Medicare Part B and packaged in single-dose containers or single-use packages, for units of discarded drug reimbursed by Medicare Part B in excess of ten percent of total allowed charges under Medicare Part B for that drug.
However, certain raw materials are only available from a single source.
Our ability to maintain and increase net sales from these products depends on several factors, including:

We rely on a combination of patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets and proprietary information, including confidential business information, show-how and know-how, in addition to any market exclusivity gained from the regulatory approval process to support our business strategy.
We also rely on trade secrets and proprietary know-how to protect the commercial viability and value of Acthar Gel.
Our business depends on the continued effectiveness and availability of our information technology infrastructure, and failures of this infrastructure could harm our operations.

In addition, we rely on third-party suppliers, manufacturers, distributors and collaboration partners to provide services for certain core aspects of our business, including supply and manufacture of key starting materials, components and APIs used in our products and in our product development activities, packaging, shipping, warehousing and distribution.
Several of our products (including our key products) and their components are manufactured by a single source, at a single manufacturing facility or stored at a single storage site.

Our ability to make scheduled payments on or to refinance our going-forward debt obligations and Acthar Gel-Related Litigation Settlement obligation depends on our financial condition and operating performance, which are subject to prevailing economic and competitive conditions and to certain financial, business, legislative, regulatory and other factors beyond our control.

The proposed listing and public offering necessarily depend on variety of factors, including market, geopolitical, industry and macroeconomic conditions, the NYSE and SEC review processes, as well as our ability to achieve our business and strategic goals.

For further discussion, see the risk factor captioned “ Our business depends on the continued effectiveness and availability of our information technology infrastructure, and failures of this infrastructure could harm our operations ” included within Item 1A.

Our principal sources of liquidity are cash generated from operations and access to our $400 million revolving credit facility, net of $4.0 million of outstanding standby letters of credit, which remains undrawn at December 31, 2025.
These valuations rely on a number of factors including operating results, business plans, economic projections, anticipated future cash flows, transactions and market place data.

The extent to which certain global macroeconomic conditions, including, but not limited to, those related to inflation and supply chain, may continue to impact the Company’s business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations, in particular, will depend on future developments which are highly uncertain and many of which are outside the Company’s control.

s.t: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company divested all of its ownership interest in Silence for proceeds of $ 10.2 million, resulting in a realized gain of $ 0.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, included within other income (expense), net in the Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations.

Other income during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 primarily included $7.7 million of income under transition services agreements related to the Separation, the sale of the Disposal Group and the Therakos Divestiture, as well as $0.6 million of realized gains on the sale of our investment in Silence Therapeutics plc. Other income for the nine months ended September 26, 2025 primarily included $6.8 million of income under the transition services agreement related to the Therakos Divestiture, partially offset by $2.6 million of unrealized losses on equity securities related to our investments in Silence Therapeutics plc and Panbela Therapeutics, Inc.

Other income for the three months ended September 26, 2025 included $1.6 million of income under the transition services agreement related to the Therakos Divestiture and $0.4 million of unrealized gains on equity securities related to our investments in Silence Therapeutics plc and Panbela Therapeutics, Inc.

Other income during 2025 primarily reflects income of $9.5 million associated with the Therakos TSA and the Par Health TSA, partially offset by $5.3 million of unrealized losses related to the changes in fair value of derivative assets and liabilities and $1.7 million of unrealized losses related to our investment in Silence Therapeutics.

Other expense in 2024 primarily relates to $17.4 million of unrealized losses on equity securities related to our investments in Silence Therapeutics plc, offset by a $7.6 million unrealized gain related to the changes in fair value of derivative assets and liabilities as discussed further in Note 21 to the Consolidated Financial Statements included in Item 8.
